summary: The Sepsis-3 criteria calculator returns vasopressors required to maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg? from the 4 fields on the form. No sign-up, no page reload, and the relationship behind it is printed below. That makes it useful for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. The results leave the screen the moment you edit a field; press Calculate and they come back updated, so a single changed input shows its own effect.

sections.title: How does the Sepsis-3 criteria calculator work?
sections.html:
The Sepsis-3 criteria calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports vasopressors required to maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg? in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the QSOFA score, the SOFA score and the serum lactate level); then you type in the septic shock.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Sepsis-3 criteria calculator
sections.html:
One relationship drives the whole page:

Vasopressors required to maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg?=-serum lactate level − QSOFA score + septic shock − SOFA score

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.html:

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Sepsis-3 criteria calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Any time the same 1 figures keep coming back — the septic shock — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

sections.title: What are the limits worth knowing?
sections.html:
Every tool draws a boundary somewhere. For the Sepsis-3 criteria calculator, these are the ones that matter:

  • The 4 drop-downs on this page offer a fixed list of cases. A value that is not on the list cannot be entered, and the nearest option is not always a good substitute.
  • The calculator reports what the relationship implies; it does not judge whether the inputs themselves are sensible, so a figure that is out by a factor of ten will produce an answer that is out by the same factor.

faq.q: What does the Sepsis-3 criteria calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns vasopressors required to maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg?, derived from the septic shock. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Sepsis-3 criteria calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the septic shock, which is 4 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (4 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Septic shock = 0. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Sepsis-3 criteria calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
